findings.name_whole_policy: 431=40 windup+12 active+40 recovery=92 ticks, impact40. Mark follows valid target only through age35, then locks36..40. Server impact creates actual falling pen at mark+5Y, not damage from eye or brush mesh. Eye scales pulse1.12 at12/24/36; ledgers open to +/-45 by6, hold36, close40. Brush swivel alternates during naming then resets32. Renderer world-text ages0..11 death2,12..23 death1,24..39 death; bright at12..14,24..26,36..39. This is finite cast, not a new font or object-production task.
findings.strokes_whole_policy: 432=10+40+34=84 ticks, emits at10/18/26/34/42 in -20/-10/0/+10/+20 degrees from fixed cast direction. Brush local yaw has corresponding five authored directions at those ticks; server spawn is calculated in world coordinates, so exact nib-contact alignment is not proven. Ledger opens +/-25 at10, holds50 and closes64. Max7 owned JudgeSpell objects gate creation; effect cut has bounded16 distinct hit UUIDs and80-tick life, no new blade asset work.
findings.cage_whole_policy: 433=16+160+36=212 ticks. Ledger opens +/-90 by12, holds through176, closes190. Lamp XZ scale1.2 at16..176, resets212. During age16..175 actor may navigate toward fixed mark at.6 when AI enabled; it keeps CAGE clip rather than walk. At176 clears owned cages. Before16/after175 horizontal motion is stopped. This is a sliding possessed book, not a hidden human walk conversion.
findings.cage_break_and_interrupt: Accepted server hurt while CAGE active from living attacker with horizontal normalized attacker offset dot cast direction<-.5 stops35 and clears cages. No damage threshold for this existing back-hit break. Otherwise actual health loss>=8 during WINDUP stops25. Ordinary stop clears cages only; already emitted non-cage pens/strokes remain bounded by their own lifetime. Time gap/reversal or death clears all owned spells. Do not claim every spell discard cancels actor.
findings.cage_producer_lifecycle: JudgeSpell cage validates alive owner, same cast epoch/current CAGE, loaded bounds and age<160; a gap>1/reversal or distance>68 discards. Captures at most8 alive noncreative nonspectator players, uses radius2.6 for confinement, maintains last legal position, native same-level connection teleport preserves view, and calls breakCage if projected/fallback position unsafe. Other discard causes do not all call breakCage. Actual networking and legality remain native acceptance.
findings.death_and_hierarchy: Death cancels body action/navigation/target/all spells; root does not undergo vanilla whole-body roll. Server removes at84 ticks, clip4.2sec. Iron spine shrinks to0 and movesY-15 by22; ledger children flare +/-150 by24. Broken brush tip rotates6..16 but inherits shrinking spine: not proof of independently visible detached debris after22. Inkstone expandsXZ1.3 by24, holds60, disappears84. Six butterfly roots are independent root children, visible only dead, grow0->1 at6..10, hold56, then0at84 while rising in distinct positions; wing curves +/-55 alternate17 keys, all six pairs use same curves. Six butterflies are one authored death mechanism, not six reference credits.
findings.reload_and_controller: Stores EliteAttack, finite bounded landing offsets, LastCombatTick/death/loot/home. Invalid landing cancels; alive load syncs, dead load clears skill. Active next combat tick with gap>1/reversal cancels and clears all spells. Cage trapped-player map is not persisted; cage load sets born=-1 so it is discarded rather than restoring constraints. Actor and object reload need combined native testing; no seamless continuation claim. START change force-resets body controller; running skill/death uses world-age tick, reused shared clock/controller evidence not new reference.
findings.whole_policy_comparison: Reuses completed InkAssassin policy: four owned matching-cast anchors break a field and stop30, whereas this single cage can break from back-hit/unsafe player correction and permits actor navigation while ledger remains spread. Both retain cast identity/time-gap guards, but those shared safeguards are not additional implementation credit.
